rule.title: Restrict Mocking to Out-of-Process Unmanaged Dependencies
rule.statement: Only mock external, out-of-process unmanaged dependencies that you do not own (e.g., Gemini API, DeepSeek API, Nodemailer). Do not mock internal classes, helpers, or managed databases.
rule.rationale: Over-mocking internal classes couples tests to private implementation details, creating brittle tests that break on every refactor without catching real bugs.
rule.implementation_guidance: Use real domain classes and in-process collaborators in unit tests. Mock only network boundaries with third-party servers.

forbidden.example: vi.mock('../utils/math-helper'); // Anti-pattern: mocking internal pure helper function

source.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
source.evidence_quote: Mock only unmanaged dependencies—dependencies with which you communicate through external APIs that you do not control. Never mock internal domain classes or managed dependencies.

rule.title: Verify State and Output, Never Interaction Counts on Internals
rule.statement: Tests must not assert internal method invocation counts (e.g. expect(internalHelper).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)) on internal components.
rule.rationale: Asserting how many times internal sub-routines are called binds tests to exact line-by-line coding choices, causing false test failures during refactoring.
rule.implementation_guidance: Assert the observable return value or the resulting database/state change.

source.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
source.evidence_quote: Verifying internal interactions leaks implementation details into tests. Tests should verify observable behavior: the output values and resulting state changes.

rule.title: Strict Test Double Taxonomy: Prefer Fakes and Stubs Over Interaction Mocks
rule.statement: Test suites must distinguish between Fakes (lightweight in-memory implementations), Stubs (canned queries), and Mocks (interaction verification). Prefer Fakes and Stubs over brittle interaction Mocks.
rule.rationale: Asserting that a specific collaborator method was called exactly N times (mocking) couples the test to procedural call sequences rather than validating final output state.
rule.implementation_guidance: Create an InMemoryUserRepository implementing UserRepository for hermetic tests. Use Mocks only to verify unobservable outgoing commands to external boundaries (e.g. email service).

preferred.example: const fakeRepo = new InMemoryUserRepository(); const service = new UserService(fakeRepo); expect(await service.getUser(id)).toEqual(expected);

source.section: Fakes, Stubs, and Mocks in Practice
source.evidence_quote: Prefer real implementations or in-memory fakes over mocks. Mocks often lead to brittle tests that break on refactoring without finding real bugs.
